rounds.note: Finite-cutoff charge terms are screened local proxies, not Ewald energies. Missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å; missing electron affinities use zero; unavailable contacts return zero.

Adaptive shells use d ≤ 1.25 dmin within the supplied 6 Å neighbors. Charge terms are screened proxies, not oxidation states or Ewald energies; missing radii use 1.3 Å and missing affinities use zero.
Adaptive shells use d ≤ 1.25 dmin within 6 Å; missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å; atomic-energy averages omit missing pairs, and screened polarity is not an electrostatic energy.

Adaptive shells use d ≤ 1.25 dmin within 6 Å. Missing radii use 1.3 Å and affinities use zero; other missing atomic values are omitted. Polarity and transfer-cost terms are local proxies, not electrostatic or formation energies.

Adaptive shells use d ≤ 1.25 dmin within 6 Å. Missing radii use 1.3 Å and affinities use zero; missing electronegativities are omitted. Contact polarity and transfer costs are proxies, not electrostatic energies.
Finite 6 Å neighborhoods include periodic images; missing radii use 1.3 Å, missing affinities use zero, and geometric contact weights are not bond orders.

Periodic contacts extend to 6 Å; finite clusters depend on the covalent cutoff. Missing radii use 1.3 Å and affinities use zero. H3 valence counts are not oxidation states; contact weights are not bond orders.

Periodic contacts are limited to 6 Å; missing radii use 1.3 Å and affinities use zero. Octet balance, short-contact contraction, and directional imbalance are structural proxies, not oxidation states, bond orders, or energies.

Group-15 coordination and linear-center scores distinguish homonuclear motifs without assigning molecular identities; 6 Å neighborhoods and covalent cutoffs remain geometric proxies, with missing radii set to 1.3 Å.
Homonuclear valence compensation is a radius-based octet proxy, not an oxidation-state assignment; periodic neighbors stop at 6 Å and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.
Distance-derived bond orders and octet residuals are proxies, not oxidation states; atomic transfer costs omit screening, neighborhoods end at 6 Å, and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.
Distance-derived bond orders and octet balances are geometric proxies, not oxidation states; new bond-order terms omit missing radii and count periodic images within 6 Å.
Bond orders and charge balances are geometric proxies, not oxidation states; neighborhoods end at 6 Å, and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.
Radius-derived bond orders and electron balances are geometric proxies, not oxidation states; periodic neighborhoods end at 6 Å and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.
Octet demand and electron-transfer terms are geometric/free-atom proxies, not oxidation states or formation energies; contacts are limited to the supplied 6 Å neighborhood.
Bond orders, metallic-site assignments and covalent-sphere packing are proxies, not oxidation states or energies; contacts end at 6 Å, and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.

Octet balance and Mulliken polarization are proxies, not oxidation states; connectivity uses radius-threshold edges within the supplied 6 Å neighborhood, with missing covalent radii replaced by 1.3 Å.
Octet residuals, metallic assignments and atomic polarization are proxies, not oxidation states or formation energies; contacts stop at 6 Å and missing covalent radii use 1.3 Å.
